steps.text:
Unfortunately, I can’t see your specific workspace or verify link status from here, so I can’t tell you categorically whether the older invite link is broken. However, these points based on product behavior may help:

- As an invitee, you sign in with the intended account (the one you want to be associated with) and accept the invitation. If the newer link is valid, sign‑in with the appropriate TableCards account and it should work.
- Duplicate invitation links can exist in the same environment (untracked by our catalog). It’s generally okay to use only the freshest link and not try to reuse or re‑use an earlier one; newer handles often take precedence over older ones in practice.
- If sign‑in fails with the new link as well, I’d defer to our human support team for account‑side checks, since I’m not able to verify permissions or link lifecycles directly. If you send a screenshot of the error and the Google sign‑in context (account you’re using and any workspace name visible), a support person can investigate faster.
- If your workspace is an invited Studio team, reissuing the invitation from your side can invalidate the earlier link—using that newer invitation is the typical workaround.

2) If that still fails, open an account‑specific help page or support request, and include:
   - The error text or screenshot
   - The Google account you used when following the link

That way a support agent can avoid the bot limitations and check your workspace’s invitation state directly.

1) With the newest link, click it in your browser, sign in to TableCards using the account you want to join, and accept the invitation.

   - The Google account you used when following the link

That way a support agent can avoid the bot limitations and check your workspace’s invitation state directly.
